newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended a quiet day's trading moderately firmer on Thursday, recouping morning gains after a brief flurry of activity on the release of U.S. PPI data pushed the market lower in line with U.S. Treasuries.
"We dipped along with Treasuries when the numbers came out but then bounced back," a dealer said, adding the professionally driven trade had largely tracked bund futures.

The U.S. monthly producer price index rose 0.3 percent in August, topping analysts' expectations of an 0.1 percent rise. But the core figure (excluding food and energy) was down 0.1 percent, versus the expected 0.1 percent rise.
The data had been seen as a clue to interest rate direction.
Another dealer said the market had already largely factored in a hike of some 25 basis points in the U.S. federal funds rate, describing underlying sentiment as "cautiously optimistic".
"The market is prepared to assume prices could go higher, and it was confirmed in that view by Buba's cautious noises on the German economic outlook," he said.
Dealers reported some lengthening trades at the short end of the curve, with activity focusing on 1999 and Sept 2002 paper.
Sept 2002 paper closed the session up 10 at 100.95 for a bid yield of 5.57 percent.
However some players were hanging back ahead of the release of U.S. consumer spending data on Friday. Dutch CPI numbers, due out at 0830 GMT, would have less of an impact, dealers said.
